explain: _hic_ is “this” for a masculine noun as the subject. _vir_ is masculine, so _hic vir_.
distractors: _hunc_ is accusative (the thing seen). A subject needs the nominative: _hic_.

explain: _haec_ is “this” for a feminine noun. _puella_ is feminine, so _haec puella_.
distractors: _hanc_ is accusative (the thing seen). A subject needs the nominative: _haec_.

explain: _hoc_ is “this” for a neuter noun. _verbum_ is neuter, so _hoc verbum_.
distractors: _hunc_ is masculine accusative. A neuter subject needs _hoc_.

explain: The man is the thing seen, so _virum_ and _hunc_ are both accusative.
distractors: _hic_ is nominative: the one doing. The thing seen is accusative: _hunc_.
_huic_ is dative (“to this”). The thing seen is accusative: _hunc_.

explain: The girl is the thing seen, so _puellam_ and _hanc_ are both accusative feminine.
distractors: _haec_ is nominative. The thing seen is accusative: _hanc_.
_huic_ is dative (“to this”). The thing seen is accusative: _hanc_.

en: I give this book to this boy.
explain: _huic_ is the dative of _hic_: “to this”. The boy receives the book, so _huic puerō_ (dative) and _hunc librum_ (accusative).
distractors: _hunc_ is accusative. The one receiving is dative: _huic_.
_hic_ is nominative. The one receiving is dative: _huic_.
_huius_ is genitive (“of this”). To this boy is dative: _huic_.

en: The face of this man is good.
explain: _huius_ is the genitive of _hic_ (“of this”), for all three genders. It goes with _virī_, which is also genitive.
distractors: _hunc_ is accusative. “Of this man” is genitive: _huius_.
_huic_ is dative (“to this”). “Of this man” is genitive: _huius_.
_hic_ is nominative. “Of this man” is genitive: _huius_.

explain: _hī_ is “these” for masculine plural nouns as the subject. _virī_ is masculine plural nominative.
distractors: _hae_ is feminine plural (“these women”). _virī_ is masculine: _hī_.
_haec_ is neuter plural (“these things”). _virī_ is masculine: _hī_.
_hōs_ is accusative plural (the things seen). A subject needs _hī_.

explain: In the neuter plural, _hic_ and the adjective both end in _-a_: _haec bona_ (these good things). _haec_ is also the feminine singular, but here the plural meaning is clear.
distractors: _hōs_ is masculine accusative plural. The subject needs the nominative: _haec_.

explain: _in_ meaning “in” takes the ablative. _urbe_ is ablative feminine, so “this” is _hāc_.
distractors: _hōc_ is ablative masculine or neuter. _urbe_ is feminine: _hāc_.
_hanc_ is accusative. After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _hāc_.
_huius_ is genitive (“of this”). After _in_ meaning “in”, use the ablative: _hāc_.

explain: The tool you use goes in the ablative: _gladiō_. The pronoun agrees: _hōc_ (masculine ablative).
distractors: _hunc_ is accusative. A tool takes the ablative: _hōc gladiō_.
_hic_ is nominative. A tool takes the ablative: _hōc gladiō_.
_hōs_ is accusative plural. A single sword is ablative singular: _hōc_.
